messages:
devon: Heads up — saw repeated 95/99p latency cliffs on shared-pool eu-west-1 overnight. Correlates with a single tenant doing large embed-batch jobs (tenant-42).

mike: ugh. which metric you looking at? can you paste the query?

devon: quick excerpt from the dashboard:
```
# top by tokens_processed per 5m
sum(rate(tokens_processed[5m])) by (tenant)
--> tenant-42 ~ 6x baseline for 03:00-06:00 UTC
95p_latency_eu_west1 spikes from 200ms -> 2.1s
```

ana: (typo: ana) this screams noisy-neighbor embedding bursts. we should consider admission tokens + isolate cheap KV cache lanes.

sam: note: soft-preempt has been on for shared-pool but locality is killing KV hitrate — when tenant-42 hops around racks we thrash the prefix cache.

jordan: can we try a two-prong approach: 1) immediate soft limit on concurrent embed batches per tenant; 2) short experiment in staging with weighted token buckets + rack-affinity? i can own the staging run.

deploy-bot: [autoscaler] applied config change: heuristics/burst_detector v2 -> enabled on eu-west-1 shared-pool at 2025-11-02T09:18:12Z

lisa: also add these telemetry tweaks before rollout: tenant-level tail-latency histogram (p99.9) and a "drop_reason" tag for admission control decisions so we can tell throttles vs rejection.

devon: for immediate mitigation i'm proposing: `rlctl set-tenant-limit tenant-42 100 --scope=eu-west-1` (concurrent embed batches) and enable rack-affinity = prefer-local. who can push now?

mike: i can push the rlctl change at 09:15 UTC and watch SLOs. will rollback if error rate goes up.

devon: thanks — i'll open a quick dashboard and add the p99.9 histogram. after we stabilise we should plan a longer-term fairshare: token-buckets where weight = committed qps + safety floor for small tenants.

sam: agreed. also need a cost check — if we start moving noisy tenants into soft-reserved capacity the bill jumps. put a cost-estimate in the rollout playbook.

jordan: i'll schedule the staging experiment and ping infra on the playbook.

devon: perfect. will follow up with a short writeup and action items. :eyes:
